description: §47.1.1 (S457 "a for __scrml_") — `__scrml_` text in a comment, a string or markup text is not a name and does not fire, and neither do the parser's own placeholders: `is some` inside a block-bodied callback (#1333) compiles clean and runs, so @msg becomes "some" after one click. (-neg: the code does not fire.)
rationale: §47.1.1 S457 ruling: the `__scrml_` reservation is decided on the parsed tree like `_scrml_` — string literals, comments and markup text are not inspected — and the expression parser's own placeholders carry a per-compilation unguessable token, which is the only exemption, so `is some` inside a callback compiles. §42.2.2a: `v is some` is true for 5.
